title: Sparsomycin inhibits translation through a conserved mechanism across all domains of life.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Queried the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA, the public sequence repository) listing for project PRJEB111032: it holds exactly 12 raw paired-end FASTQ.gz files (6 runs = 3 untreated + 3 sparsomycin-treated 'iTP-Seq library' samples), 114,598,832 reads total, 8.59 GB compressed, and the 'analysis' (processed-file) query returns an empty table. Confirmed PDB entry 12DP exists via the RCSB (Protein Data Bank) REST API. Confirmed the open-access full text contains zero mentions of 'Supplementary <anything>' and Europe PMC reports hasSuppl = N; the supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out on its one attempt.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Library design (short open reading frames with 15 random NNN codons, ~10^12 sequences, translated in vitro with PURExpress lacking release factor 2), drug concentration (100 microM sparsomycin), the finding that ribosome density nearly vanishes after codon 5 under drug, and the reported amino-acid context effects (aromatic Phe/Tyr at nascent-chain positions -3/-2 enhance stalling). None of these numbers were checked in files because no processed file exists.

a1_downloadable.note: ENA project PRJEB111032 is open, no login or application; however the only files are raw sequencing reads (12 FASTQ.gz, 8.59 GB), which this project's own rules forbid downloading, and each file is far over the 50 MB cap.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The prediction target (sparsomycin-dependent ribosome stalling per nascent-peptide context) exists in no file. It must be built from 114.6 million raw read pairs by running the assay-specific itpseq pipeline: trim, infer inverse-toeprint length, translate, aggregate per amino-acid context, then compute treated-versus-untreated enrichment. The paper's Figure 2C/2D enrichment heatmaps were never deposited as tables.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not scored further (stopped at A2). The peptide-coding sequences are inside the reads themselves, so inputs would be present once reads were processed; nothing needs external identifier lookup.

a4_units_stated.note: Not scored further. Paper states read distributions in reads per million and enrichment as treated/untreated ratios, but no units exist in any deposited file because no table was deposited.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not scored further. 114,598,832 reads were verified in the ENA listing; how many distinct peptide contexts survive filtering and replicate-consistency is unknown, since that count only appears after processing.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Borderline FAIL: 8.59 GB compressed FASTQ (verified in ENA), roughly 25-30 GB uncompressed, versus the ~5 GB working-set limit. Streaming would work in principle but the whole pipeline must be run before a single labelled row exists.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable. Six libraries in ENA match the three-plus-three replicate design described in the paper; no row counts exist to compare against because no processed table was deposited.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not scored further. The label would trace to a real physical measurement (sequencing of RNase R-protected mRNA fragments), not another model's output, so A8 itself is clean - the problem is purely that the label must be constructed.

existing_models.name: Riboformer (deep learning model of context-dependent ribosome translation dynamics, Nature Communications 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Only the search-result summary was retrieved, not the paper; no score or split verified here.

existing_models.name: ROSE (convolutional network predicting ribosome stalling from coding sequence)
existing_models.score_and_split: Only search-result summary retrieved; score and split not verified.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) on the short nascent peptide, or a small convolutional network on codons
backbone.hardware: CPU-only would be fine for 15-residue peptides, but the question is moot while no labelled table exists

integration.partner_dataset: Earlier inverse-toeprinting datasets from the same lab (chloramphenicol/erythromycin, Seip et al. 2018; tetracenomycin X, Leroy et al. 2023), joinable on the identical (NNN)15 random-library peptide context
integration.join_key: nascent peptide sequence at positions -3 to +1 relative to the ribosome's catalytic centre
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do different ribosome-targeting antibiotics share a common nascent-peptide grammar for when they stall the ribosome, or is each drug's context specificity its own code?

controls.positive_control: The paper's own reported effect - aromatic residues (Phe, Tyr) at nascent-chain positions -3/-2 enhance sparsomycin stalling - must be recovered by any model.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the treated/untreated label across contexts; enrichment signal must collapse to the replicate-noise level.
controls.external_validation: Hold out one of the three biological replicates, and test transfer to the published chloramphenicol/tetracenomycin iTP-seq libraries.

honest_claim_h3: A model could claim only: among short random 15-codon open reading frames translated in a reconstituted E. coli in vitro system at 100 microM sparsomycin, the nascent peptide sequence predicts how much drug-dependent ribosome stalling is seen - with no claim about natural genes, living cells, or other drug concentrations.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the growing peptide's sequence to predict how strongly an antibiotic stalls the ribosome at that position.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be a short nascent peptide context (the last few amino acids made before the ribosome paused) from a library of random sequences; the number of usable examples is unknown because no processed table was deposited.
plain_idea.predict: How much more (or less) often ribosomes pause at that context when sparsomycin is present, measured as the ratio of sequencing counts between drug-treated and untreated reactions in an inverse-toeprinting experiment.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Medicinal chemists redesigning sparsomycin would learn which peptide neighbours strengthen the drug's grip, and a shared grammar across antibiotics would be real biology even if prediction is mediocre.

label_elsewhere.sources: Not filled in detail because the verdict is reject; sparsomycin-specific stalling enrichment is measured only in this paper, though related antibiotic stalling landscapes exist in earlier Innis-lab inverse-toeprinting papers.
label_elsewhere.why: The label is drug- and assay-specific, so no public resource holds it for other items.

ml_idea: Predict sparsomycin-dependent ribosome stalling strength from the nascent peptide sequence, using the paper's inverse-toeprinting sequencing of a random 15-codon open reading frame library (3 treated, 3 untreated replicates), with transfer to other antibiotics' stalling landscapes as the headline question. Blocked because only raw reads were deposited.

effort.compute_note: Sizes are the verified ENA byte counts (8.59 GB compressed FASTQ, 114.6M reads); the 30-hour and 6 GB figures are estimates for downloading and running the itpseq pipeline end to end on a CPU laptop, nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query the ENA file report for processed/analysis objects on PRJEB111032 - it returns an empty table, so only raw FASTQ exists. One call, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: A2 fails: the only data deposited is 12 raw FASTQ files (8.59 GB, 114.6M reads) plus two crystal structures, so the stalling label must be built from scratch with an assay-specific pipeline before any modelling can start; A6 also fails on working-set size, and this project's rules forbid downloading raw sequencing data.
